targeting_gate.verbatim_anchor:
In semiarid
environments with inadequate water (< 1000 mm rainfall yr–1) and on acid
infertile soils, hedgerows produce too little biomass and/or become too
competitive to benefit crops. If (C) is substantially reduced, HI may increase
crop yields in some of these situations, even for a relatively small (F), but
the necessary management of hedges could be too intensive to be practical.
On acid soils, HI may give a positive response over the long term and with
external inputs (lime and P fertilizer), but many small farmers may not cope
with these requirements.
In agroclimates where HI is suitable, it can provide most of the N needed
for moderate yields of cereals, but it will not supply adequate N or P to realize
maximum yields. HI does not seem appropriate for tuber crops and cotton.
Sustainable production from HI requires P fertilization and use of deep-rooted,
N2-fixing trees. Leucaena and gliricidia are well suited for base-rich soils,
whereas calliandra, Acacia auriculiformis, peltophorum, dactyladenia, eryth-
rina, L. diversifolia and inga are suited for acid soils in specific climatic
conditions.
